articles.title: UK diesel price hits record high of £2 a litre
articles.summary: Motorists and small businesses struggle with costs as Iran war drives up cost of oil worldwide

blocks.text: British motorists face more pressure at the pumps after the average price of diesel climbed to a record £2 a litre.

The price at UK forecourts has risen sharply since late February, when the US-Israel war on Iran began disrupting supplies of crude and refined oil products from the Gulf, leading to cost increases across the economy.
The RAC motoring group said on Friday that the average price had reached 200.01p a litre, meaning the cost of filling up an average family car is now £110, nearly £32 more than before the Iran war.
Simon Williams, head of policy at the RAC, said: “This is a pump price threshold that no one wanted to cross.”

Earlier on Friday the transport minister, Keir Mather, sought to avert panic at the pumps, insisting that the UK is not facing a diesel shortage after Donald Trump threatened to cut off US supplies of the fuel.
Motorists and small businesses have been struggling with the increasing cost of filling up.
after newsletter promotion
The fresh high was recorded after record fuel prices across Europe in recent weeks, which have ignited calls for political leaders to take action to protect consumers against rising cost pressures.
Inflation in the cost of road fuels has outpaced the surge in global oil markets due to a sharp drop in output from refineries damaged by war in the Middle East and in Russia.

Before the Ukraine war, Russia provided between 10% and 15% of the world’s diesel supplies. Another 10% of global diesel supplies transited through the strait of Hormuz from Gulf nations before Iran responded to the US-Israeli attacks by disrupting the strait.

articles.title: Trillanes to Escudero: Focus on evidence, not technicalities in Sara Duterte trial
articles.summary: Former Senator Antonio Trillanes IV urged Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero to prioritize the presentation of evidence over technicalities in the impeachment trial of Vice…

blocks.text: Published October 2, 2026 6:20pm

Former Senator Antonio Trillanes IV urged Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero to prioritize the presentation of evidence over technicalities in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

Trillanes made the remarks a day after the prosecution dropped him from its list of witnesses. He later said he was the one who asked the prosecution to remove his name, saying he felt unwelcome before the Senate impeachment court after Escudero declined to issue him a subpoena.

“Iyong presiding officer lang naman ’yung nagtitimon. So kung boring ’yung impeachment trial, it’s the fault entirely of the presiding officer. Kapag tinrato mo itong parang criminal court, ganyan ang mangyayari,” Trillanes said.
(It is the presiding officer who calls the shots. If the impeachment trial becomes boring, that's on him. If you make it akin to a criminal court, that is what will happen.)

“Mahigit 30 na kaso na rin ang kinaharap ko eh. I have lived it; it can be boring talaga. But that should not be the case for the impeachment court. Dapat hinahanap nila 'yung katotohanan. Hindi naman ito criminal trial na may kulong," Trillanes added.
(I have faced around 30 cases myself, and the trial could get boring. But the impeachment court should search for the truth. This is not a criminal trial, where the punishment is jail time.)
Trillanes then reiterated his previous position that it should be Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian who should be the presiding officer for a more understandable approach on issues at hand.
“That is why I was pushing for Senator Sherwin as presiding officer because he has a layman mindset. But they were saying that it has to be a lawyer. No, we don’t need a lawyer here,” Trillanes said.
“Kailangan lang dito may bukas na pag-iisip na kailangan hanapin yung katotohanan. Ganoon lang po yun,” Trillanes added.
(What we need is someone who is willing to search for the truth. It is that simple.)

Trillanes cited the recent deferment of the presentation of Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura of the Anti-Money Laundering Council as a witness for the prosecution, with presiding officer Escudero granting the defense’s request for more time to prepare.

“Napagbotohan na nila ’yan. Nag-agree na sila diyan. Kung objective ang presiding officer, tapos na yan. Present niyo na yan. Tapos may kopya na sila. Kailangan [raw] nila (defense) ng oras. Parang sounds reasonable, right? Pero hawak na nila ‘yung mga dokumento na ’yon weeks before. Pero kinatigan sila ng presiding officer,” Trillanes said.

(They already voted on it that the presentation of AMLC, bank records are allowed. The witness from AMLC should have presented already. Both parties already have copies of these. The defense said they needed time. It sounds reasonable, but they already have the documents way back. And yet the presiding officer ruled in their favor.)
“E di nagsayang ng isa't kalahating araw. So bantayan nyo yung presiding officer. That's what I'm saying. Tingnan nyo. Kung boring, problema niya ‘yun,” Trillanes added.
(A day was wasted. So you should keep watch on the presiding officer. Observe keenly. If it gets boring, that's on him.)

The prosecution is presenting evidence for Article 2 of the impeachment case against the Vice President, which alleges unexplained wealth stemming from her purported failure to truthfully disclose her assets in her Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs) and to divest from businesses, as required of the President and Vice President under the Constitution. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: A 'dark cloud' and 'dismal' mood: How it feels on Cornell campus right now
articles.summary: Students tell the BBC that the tension on campus has become palpable since allegations from 2024 resurfaced.

blocks.text: A 'dark cloud' and 'dismal' mood: How it feels on Cornell campus right now
Cornell students voice frustration at public hearing over rape case
ByNada TawfikNew York correspondent at Cornell University and Sakshi Venkatraman

Under normal circumstances, Cornell University is a beautiful place to study at this time of year. Autumn leaves bring pops of colour to its stately buildings, which are set against the backdrop of the rolling hills of upstate New York.

But students and faculty members say the investigation into an alleged gang rape that took place on these grounds two years ago has cast a "dark cloud" over the campus - stirring anger, concern over fraternity culture, and a backlash against the university's handling of the situation.
Students and staff at the Ivy League university spoke to the BBC, some on condition of anonymity, saying the tension on campus had become palpable since the 2024 case resurfaced in recent weeks.
At a student assembly on Thursday, which was organised to allow students to voice their concerns, many called for drastic change at the university.
Others labelled the perceived lack of justice a "disgrace" and said they felt ashamed of the prestigious university, which has defended its handling of the case.
"We deserve to know that our institution values our safety more than its reputation," undergraduate Sophia Riley Sim told those at the gathering.
Sim said she had been too upset by the case to attend classes for the past week.

blocks.caption: Image caption, The campus of Cornell University in Ithaca, New York

blocks.text: Image source, Getty Images
The campus of Cornell University in Ithaca, New York

The accuser at the centre of the alleged gang rape, known anonymously as Jane Doe, filed a civil lawsuit against Cornell on 16 September, saying she was drugged and raped at a fraternity house in 2024.
She claimed that Cornell had failed to protect her or adequately punish the men involved in the incident. The men have been dubbed the Cornell Seven.
Cornell has already agreed to an independent investigation into the rape allegation.

The university has also defended its handling of the issue to date, external, saying it conducted an "extensive investigation" that lasted several months following the report of the incident, and that it followed applicable federal civil rights law.
Shortly after Thursday's student assembly at Cornell, New York Governor Kathy Hochul announced she had appointed the state attorney general, Letitia James, as special prosecutor in the case.
She said she had "lost faith" in the Tompkins County district attorney, who was previously leading the investigation. James therefore takes over the case from Matthew Van Houten.

Van Houten's office initially concluded that the evidence did not meet the legal threshold to bring charges - before reopening a criminal investigation last week in light of the new civil complaint, a move that Cornell supported.
The upcoming "Justice for Survivors" protest, planned at the university for 5 October, is being advertised in flyers all over campus. It calls on Cornell to take action against alleged rape culture.

Student organisers are calling for Cornell to expel and revoke the degrees of the alleged perpetrators of the rape, rewrite policies around sexual assault punishments, initiate an external investigation of the university and mandate prevention training for campus police.

As part of its account of its prior investigation of the case, Cornell says: "At its conclusion, the hearing panel issued a range of sanctions, which included expulsions and suspensions from Cornell."
Cornell says it is legally prevented from publicly disclosing specific disciplinary outcomes about disciplinary students, adding that "we recognise that this legal limitation can be frustrating".
Across campus, the case has stirred anger.
One fourth-year student recalled that it had been hard to live there in 2024, in the aftermath of the incident, as rumours began spreading about Jane Doe.
Now, two years on, she told the BBC how she and her friends felt "overwhelmed" and "disappointed", comparing the atmosphere on campus to a "dark cloud". Cornell, she believes, mishandled things.
She wants the administration to admit what she sees as its mistakes, calling the lack of transparency disheartening.

She also asked why multiple men in a group chat for members of Chi Phi - the fraternity group at the centre of the allegations - did not speak up. A chapter of the fraternity was closed in 2024 and remains barred from campus.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Students and staff have spoken of a "dark cloud" over the campus

blocks.text: Students and staff have spoken of a "dark cloud" over the campus
Students and community members also used Thursday's student assembly meeting to vent their frustrations and disappointment.
"I am very disgusted to be here, to be paying this institution to be here," freshman Eliana Dolven-Miller said. "There was a lot of anger in that room, I was very angry."
Eeshaan Chaudhuri, the student assembly chair, opened the meeting by saying that the campus stood "with victims of sexual violence".
"We don't tolerate it here on campus, and I think I can speak for every single one of us, and I can say we're absolutely ashamed of the events that happened on our campus," Chaudhuri said.

The student group has also raised a resolution calling on the university to release a written account of how it handled the alleged sexual assault, including what evidence was gathered and whether and when the university referred the matter to campus police.
"I'm very shocked" - College students react to Cornell University rape investigation
A faculty member said the mood on campus was "dismal". Staff were not trained therapists, she said, so it was hard to know how to navigate these discussions with students.

It was an "incredible situation that was so… I just don't understand," she said, adding that she was unsure if the university should have gone further, and adding that this was not the first time a fraternity group had had problems on campus.
Some of the freshmen, or first-year students, who spoke to the BBC had only arrived at Cornell last month.

A young woman said she and her friends had been discussing the allegations again that morning. Her friend said it had been difficult for him to come to an Ivy League university feeling excited about the future, only to see this story dominate the news.
Students were not OK about what happened to Jane Doe, he said.
Cornell alumni have also given their views.
More than 1,300 graduates have signed a letter calling on the university to take "swift and expansive" action after the allegations came back to light.

"Will Cornell take this as an opportunity to ask difficult questions about the proliferation of sexual violence on its own campus?" asks the letter, which was published in the university's student newspaper.
"Or will it shy away from reform to protect its image? This is not an isolated incident."

articles.title: OpenAI disclose another hack on government department in Australia
articles.summary:
Attack accessing historical data on bushfires occurred in June but not disclosed by the tech company until Thursday

  • Get our

blocks.text: Artificial intelligence company OpenAI has disclosed another unauthorised hack on a government department in Australia.
In June, an OpenAI agent hacked into a New South Wales state government department and accessed historical non-public data on bushfires without authorisation.
The breach, which comes weeks after news of a similar hack on a federal government department involving Medicare data, was not reported by the US based company until Thursday.
The NSW Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water is now working with the state’s cyber security agency to investigate the breach.
The Australian Signals Directorate has also been informed of the hack on the NSW national parks and wildlife service.
OpenAI told the NSW government that its agent had operated beyond its intended use and the statistics it obtained were not publicly available.
The company first became aware of the breach on Tuesday and conducted a 48 hours review to determine its scope before informing the NSW premier’s office.
“The results we reviewed do not show that the model retrieved any personal information,” an OpenAI spokesperson said.
This latest breach has added to calls for tougher regulation of AI companies and for bolstered cyber security defences.
“We simply cannot trust these companies. They have no respect for the sovereignty of our governments, of our way of life,” Greens MP Abigail Boyd said.
Boyd said it was damning that the breach occurred in June but the government was not notified until this week.

“We clearly cannot rely on these multinational big tech companies to comply with even the most minimal of social obligations such as notifying when, or even taking enough care to notice if, their products are hacking government systems,” Boyd said.
On Wednesday, the department of home affairs on Wednesday told federal departments to examine their older software and ensure cyber security was up to date.
The prime minister expressed his “extreme concern” about at an OpenAI agent hacking Australian Institute of Health and Welfare in June.
The Victorian Department of Health and the New South Wales Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research were also compromised by an OpenAI agent.
An artificial intelligence agent is a system that autonomously solves problems, makes decisions, plans and performs complex tasks on behalf of another user or system, using all available tools.

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Raffy Tulfo not arrested
articles.summary: Senator Raffy Tulfo was present at the Senate impeachment court days after YouTube videos falsely claimed he had been arrested

blocks.text: Claim: An arrest warrant was issued against Senator Raffy Tulfo, who was then apprehended by the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP).
Why we fact-checked this: The thumbnail of the YouTube video bearing the claim shows Tulfo alongside an image of a purported Supreme Court (SC) warrant and armed personnel from the AFP.
As of writing, the video posted on September 26 has 143,511 views, 3,800 likes, and 284 comments. Text on its thumbnail and its title read: “Raffy Tulfo may warrant! Utos ng Supreme Court sa AFP?”
(Raffy Tulfo has a warrant! Supreme Court order to the AFP?)

Another YouTube video uploaded by the same user on September 24 has 71,559 views, 2,300 likes, and 183 comments as of writing. Its thumbnail and caption state: “Raffy Tulfo inaresto ng AFP! Pinasok ang Senado?”
(Raffy Tulfo arrested by the AFP! Entered the Senate?)

The facts: Tulfo has not been arrested, and he continues to perform his duties as senator. No credible news reports, official notices from government agencies, or statements from Tulfo himself indicate that such an event happened.

Contrary to the claim, videos and live coverage show that he was present on Day 31 of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on September 29, days after the first video claimed he had allegedly been arrested.

Neither YouTube video presents evidence of a warrant, court order, or any other official notice to support the claim. Instead, both contain unrelated political commentary on corruption, confidential funds, and voting in the 2028 elections.

Supposed SC warrant: The video does not identify any case that would have led to the issuance of an alleged arrest warrant against Tulfo. For a warrant to be issued, a case must first be filed before the proper court, after which trial court judges or justices determine whether probable cause exists to issue a warrant of arrest. (READ: Indicted? Charged? A guide to court jargon)
The Supreme Court primarily exercises original jurisdiction over certain cases and the authority to review, revise, modify, or affirm lower court decisions.

Publicly available Supreme Court records reviewed as of September 30 show no issuance that supports the claim. There are likewise no reports from credible media outlets about a warrant of arrest against Tulfo or his supposed arrest.
Tulfo’s role in Duterte’s impeachment trial: The false claim began circulating while Tulfo was serving as a senator-judge in the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

As a senator-judge, Tulfo previously questioned defense lawyer Michael Poa’s role as Duterte’s counsel, citing a potential conflict of interest following the relevation that Poa — previously an undersecretary and chief of staff of the Department of Education — had met with the Commission on Audit to discuss an audit query related to confidential funds.
Tulfo has also made statements about the Vice President’s alleged business involvements.

He was also among the 13 senator-judges who voted to lower the conviction threshold to 14 votes. His brother, senator-judge Erwin Tulfo, made the motion to bar absentee senators from voting in the trial.
Debunked: Rappler has previously fact-checked false claims about the Tulfo brothers:

FACT CHECK: Raffy Tulfo not expelled from Senate
FACT CHECK: Tulfo remains a sitting senator

articles.title: Kinky dating app Feeld pays founders record £3.8m after sales jump
articles.summary: Platform ‘for the curious’ says users outside the UK account for nearly 90% of its revenues

blocks.text: Feeld, a UK-based dating app aimed at non-monogamous, queer and kinky users, has reported strong sales growth and paid its founders their largest-ever dividend as it attracts users from more “vanilla” rivals.
Revenues jumped by 24% to £64m following a surge in interest from what it called “open-minded people exploring love, desire, and alternative relationships in a safe, inclusive space”.
Pre-tax profits grew from £9.3m to £11.4m, and the company’s shareholders – including the couple who founded it – shared in a dividend of £3.8m.
Ana Kirova and her partner, Dimo Trifonov, started the business under the name 3nder (pronounced Thrinder), initially targeting couples and singles looking for threesomes.
They were forced to change the company’s name to Feeld owing to a lawsuit from Tinder but it has since experienced rapid growth even as larger rivals have faltered.

Match Group, which owns Tinder and other dating apps such as Hinge and OK Cupid, reported a 5% decline in user numbers earlier this year, amid reports of fatigue with the experience of seeking romance or sex via an app.

But Feeld, which calls itself a dating app “for the curious”, appears to be scooping up some of those users. While this has prompted reports that its edgy image has been watered down by an influx of people with more conventional or monogamous sensibilities, Feeld’s president, Kyle Brennan, said it reflected changing tastes.

“These numbers speak to something bigger than the growth of our business,” said Brennan. “They reflect a broader shift in how people are thinking about connection, with greater openness, curiosity and agency to do things differently.”
after newsletter promotion

Accounts filed at Companies House said rising sales reflected “strong global user growth”, particularly outside the UK, with the rest of the world accounting for £56m of its total £64m in revenues, nearly 90%. Mexico and Spain were Feeld’s fastest-growing regions, while New York, Toronto and Paris led the way among cities, each recording an uplift in user numbers of more than 20%, the company said.

Feeld makes money via the sale of its Majestic memberships, which give users features such as unlimited opportunities to “like” other members, the ability to see who has liked them, and advanced filters to tailor specifications for a potential partner.
It also sells members extra “pings”, a feature that allows members to express interest in someone and send them a message, without having matched with them first.
In 2024, it emerged that some of these features were temporarily vulnerable to manipulation due to security “vulnerabilities” exposed by cybersecurity experts.
Research by the London-based cybersecurity firm Fortbridge found that users could have had sensitive data including messages, private photos and details of their sexuality accessed or even edited.

At the time, Feeld said it had investigated the problems brought to its attention by Fortbridge on 3 March and fixed them by 28 May that year. It said there was no evidence that any customer data had been accessed. It has invested £10.5m in technological upgrades in the past year.
The largest dividend reported in Feeld’s previous accounts was £600,000 in 2024.

As well as its dating platform, Feeld runs in-person social events including a “kinky trivia” night and a “pitch your mate” event, at which guests take to the stage to wax lyrical about why people should date their friends.

articles.summary: The Indian airline captain who helped thwart an apparent attempt to crash a FlyDubai flight described Friday how he fought for his life in the minutes after his co-pilot stabbed him and the plane…

image.caption: Capt. Smit Machchhar, who is from Mumbai, was seriously injured in Wednesday's attack but managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to enter and restrain the attacker. (Israel's Foreign Ministry/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

The Indian airline captain who helped thwart an apparent attempt to crash a FlyDubai flight described Friday how he fought for his life in the minutes after his co-pilot stabbed him and the plane began a steep descent.
Capt. Smit Machchhar spoke to Indian PM in interview broadcast live from hospital

Capt. Smit Machchhar, recovering in an Abu Dhabi hospital, told Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in a video call broadcast live on television news channels that he knew he had to get back on his feet to save the passengers aboard the aircraft.
"I had so many wounds. I had fallen down," he said from the hospital, his head bandaged and tubes in his nose, before breaking down as he recalled the attack.
"I was fighting for my life. At one point, I realized that if I didn't get up … then passengers would lose their lives," he told Modi.

items: Passengers foil bid to crash Dubai-Tel Aviv flight after co-pilot stabbed pilot, Israel says
What we know so far about the midair FlyDubai attack

blocks.text: Machchhar, who is from India's financial hub of Mumbai, was seriously injured in Wednesday's attack but managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to enter and restrain the attacker as the Boeing 737 descended sharply, witnesses and Israeli authorities said.
He has been hailed as a hero for his actions, with world leaders saying he helped prevent a potential disaster.
Indian FlyDubai pilot hailed as hero in Mumbai
The flight, carrying 182 people from Dubai to Tel Aviv, was diverted to Tabuk in northwestern Saudi Arabia for an emergency landing.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the attacker, an Omani national, was arrested in Saudi Arabia and was undergoing interrogation there. His motive for the attack was not immediately clear.
Recited prayer for strength
Machchhar said that during those difficult moments, he recited the Hanuman Chalisa, a Hindu devotional hymn dedicated to Lord Hanuman and traditionally recited as a prayer for strength and courage.
"Lord Hanuman gave me courage," he told Modi.

Machchhar, who is married and has two children, has worked for FlyDubai for about four years, according to his LinkedIn profile. Before joining the airline, he spent 11 years with SpiceJet, an Indian low-cost carrier, where he served as a senior commander and line training captain. He logged more than 9,750 flying hours with SpiceJet.

articles.title: Monster Hunter Outlanders launches globally on October 29
articles.summary: TOKYO, Japan – Monster Hunter Outlanders will launch globally on October 29, 2026, (excluding mainland China), bringing Capcom’s iconic monster-hunting franchise to mobile devices. The game is…

blocks.text: TOKYO, Japan – Monster Hunter Outlanders will launch globally on October 29, 2026, (excluding mainland China), bringing Capcom’s iconic monster-hunting franchise to mobile devices. The game is positioned as a more accessible entry point for both longtime fans and newcomers.

While Monster Hunter Outlanders marks a significant shift for a franchise traditionally associated with PC and console gaming, both TiMi Studio Group and Capcom stressed that preserving the essence of Monster Hunter remained one of the project’s biggest priorities.
Bringing the Monster Hunter experience to mobile
According to Capcom producer Ichiro Kiyokawa, the team was particularly focused on retaining the sense of decision-making that defines encounters throughout the series.

“You need to observe the behavior of monsters and you need to judge whether to dodge or whether to attack. So by observing and making different judgments, depending on the behavior of monsters, you need to make different actions and you can also choose different weapon types as well.” said Kiyokawa, in an interview with Tech INQ during Tokyo Game Show 2026, as Monster Hunter Outlanders gave fans a chance to play a demo of the upcoming game.
That philosophy sits at the heart of Monster Hunter Outlanders, even as the game introduces systems specifically designed for mobile players.
Rather than creating a direct adaptation of existing entries, the developers sought to build a title that could stand alongside the broader franchise while offering its own identity.

For the team at TiMi Studio Group, one of the biggest challenges was finding a way to deliver the series’ signature action gameplay on smartphones without overwhelming players unfamiliar with Monster Hunter.

“To realize the gameplay of Monster Hunter IP in this brand new mobile game, especially the action experience, the biggest challenge we have faced is how we can simplify the whole mechanics and controls inside a mobile phone.” said Dong Huang, producer at Tencent’s TiMi Studio Group.
The challenge extended beyond controls. Ensuring stable performance across a broad range of mobile devices required extensive optimization work throughout development.

“It’s a mobile game, so smartphones’ performance and functionality and compatibility, that can be a challenge. So to be compatible with a smartphone, we have made a lot of optimization in terms of functionality and performance.” added Dong Huang.
RELATED STORY: Blades of Mirage puts Southeast Asia at its fantasy core
Lowering Monster Hunter’s barrier to entry

Accessibility emerged as a recurring theme throughout the beta tests of the game. Both TiMi Studio Group and Capcom recognized that the series had a high barrier to entry because of its complex systems and demanding hunts.
For those players, Monster Hunter Outlanders is intended to serve as a gateway into the series.
“When new players come to play Monster Hunter Outlanders, they can [hopefully] say, ‘Finally, I can play Monster Hunter, even though I’m not really good at action games.’” said Dong Huang.
Capcom noted that the game includes a dedicated Adventure Mode designed to simplify controls and help newcomers become comfortable with the experience.
Kiyokawa said the mobile title occupies a unique position within the franchise by lowering the barrier to entry while maintaining core Monster Hunter gameplay.

“Because it’s a mobile game, it doesn’t require any dedicated computer or dedicated console. So starting to play Monster Hunter Outlanders is much easier. So the starting hurdle will be much lower.” said Kiyokawa.
What players can expect from Monster Hunter Outlanders

Beyond adapting the franchise for mobile, the developers also highlighted content created specifically for Monster Hunter Outlanders. During the Tokyo Game Show, players were able to take on Ruger Aidal, a new Elder Dragon introduced exclusively for the game.

“We have added new elements, new monsters, original monsters inside Monster Hunter Outlanders, and we are very confident about delivering those new elements to even more users. So, after we officially release this game, please look forward to having a battle against different monsters, including this brand new original monster, Ruger Aidal, and please enjoy these new challenges.” added Kiyokawa.
TiMi Studio Group also confirmed support for controllers and joysticks, allowing players to use alternative control options during hunts.

Together with the new Elder Dragon Ruger Aidal, the developers said players can look forward to original content created specifically for Monster Hunter Outlanders, including a new story, new Adventurers, and new challenges distinct from previous entries in the franchise.
Monster Hunter Outlanders will launch globally on October 29, 2026, for iOS and Android devices, excluding mainland China.
Pre-registration is now available in both the App Store and Google Play Store.

articles.title: Ukraine: Kyiv bridges shut after fatal Russian drone assault
articles.summary: The latest Russian attacks killed at least one person and severely disrupted traffic in the Ukrainian capital. Several bridges over the Dnipro River connect western and eastern Kyiv.

image.caption: The Pivdennyi Bridge, or Southern Bridge, was one of the bridges closed as a result of the latest Russian drone attack [FILE: April 19, 2019]Image: Christophe Gateau/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Several bridges in Kyiv have been closed as the result of new Russian drone attacks which killed one person in the city, the Ukrainian capital's authorities said Friday.
There are a total of eight bridges that connect Kyiv's western and eastern banks along the Dnipro River.
What do we know about the Russian drone attack on Kyiv?
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the city's Southern Bridge, also known as the Pivdennyi Bridge, was "completely closed" to traffic.

blocks.caption: A Russian strike hit a building in the Darnytskyi District in southeastern Kyiv Image: Valentyn Ogirenko/REUTERS

blocks.text: The concrete and steel bridge carries road vehicles and a metro rail line. The Southern Bridge has been hit twice over the two days by Russian drone attacks.
The Paton Bridge was also closed to traffic towards the left bank of the Dnipro River, Klitschko said.

Russia's Ministry of Defense said its drones targeted a bridge over the Dnipro which is used for military purposes. Russia also said it attacked a power station in the surrounding Kyiv region alongside the Port of Izmail near the Black Sea and a cargo vessel.
A Russian attack on Kyiv also left one person in dead and at least two others injured after a strike hit a 25-story building in the Darnytskyi district.

Russia has frequently targeted Kyiv with overnight drone attacks in the years since the start of the February 2022 invasion. Ukraine in response has been developing interceptor technology to down those combat drones.

blocks.caption: Residents in Kyiv are frequently terrorized by nightly Russian drone attacks Image: Valentyn Ogirenko/REUTERS

blocks.text: Ukraine carries out fresh attacks on Russian oil facilities

Meanwhile, the governor of Russia's southern Volgograd region said Ukrainian drone attacks targeted industrial infrastructure. An apartment building was also damaged in the Ukrainian attack, wounding one person.
Authorities in the southern Russian region of Krasnodar said drone debris damaged an "enterprise" in the Black Sea city of Tuapse.

articles.title: France: 400 schools closed as student protests continue
articles.summary: Police have made around 2,000 arrests and scores of people have been injured as student protests spread across France. Ministers have called for a "day of dialogue" but students have called for…

image.caption: "Protest is a fundamental right," reads one placard. "You don't want to hear our words; you just fire tear gas," reads another.Image: Sarah Meyssonnier/REUTERS

blocks.text: Over 400 schools and colleges across France remained closed on Friday as student protests over education-related grievances continued — with some turning violent.

"There are over ⁠400 schools and other educational establishments that I know of that will be closed," confirmed French Education ​Minister Edouard Geffray on broadcaster ​France 2 late on Thursday night.

The protests ​against teacher shortages, dilapidated school buildings and a lack of learning materials erupted at lycées (equivalent to US high schools) in the Paris region last month before spreading across the country this week.

blocks.caption: Students are angry at what they see as a general lack of investment in their educationImage: Abdul Saboor/REUTERS

blocks.text: Student protests in France: damage, injuries, arrests
Police have made around 2,000 arrests and scores of people have been injured, including 40 high school principals, according to Geffray.
Fires were started in at least two high schools on Thursday, while teachers were reportedly inadvertently ​splashed with petrol ⁠at a third in the southern city of Marseille, according to officials.
At ​least one car was torched in the eastern city of Strasbourg while riot police clashed with youths in Toulouse in the southwest.
In the southeastern region of Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, authorities claimed that "at least €25 million" of damage has been done in their jurisdiction alone.
On Friday, more clashes between student protesters and police were reported in cities across the country, including in Loire, where several officers were injured, and in the capital Paris.
But students have also criticized what they see as a heavy-handed police response.
"You don't want to hear our words; you just fire tear gas," one student wrote on a placard outside the Lycée Voltaire in central Paris (see main photo above).
"Protest is a fundamental right," read another sign.
France students protest school conditions

Minister Geffray told broadcasters on Friday morning that "violent individuals" were "infiltrating groups of students" and "taking the movement hostage" and called on parents to prevent their children from joining the protests.
"What matters now is ensuring our children are no longer out on the streets, because they are in danger," he said.
Geffray was planning to meet with student representatives and trade unions on Friday, saying: "Today will be a day of dialogue."
France: government blames far-left LFI

According to Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu, French domestic intelligence agencies told a crisis meeting on Thursday that the movement has been initiated by politicians from the left-wing party La France Insoumise (France Unbowed or LFI) – who have denied the allegations.
Veteran LFI leader and 2027 presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon has indeed supported the protests but called on students to use non-violent methods.

"Students, teachers and educational staff are facing the same state of neglect and their positions and claims should be respected," he wrote in a statement earlier this week, calling for "disciplined struggle, no panic, no irritation."
Meanwhile, student union bodies have called for a day of mass protest next Tuesday, October 6, under the slogan: "Police out of schools! No to the repression of student mobilization!"
"The police have no place in front of educational establishments," read a statement. "We support the ongoing mobilization and call for it to be reinforced."

articles.title: Drumcree talks break up without agreement on fifth day of standoff
articles.summary:
Dispute over march will now go to legal appeal on Monday after talks hosted by Northern Ireland secretary end

Talks aimed at resolving the Drumcree parade dispute have broken up without…

blocks.text: Talks aimed at resolving the Drumcree parade dispute have broken up without agreement, with the Northern Ireland secretary, Chris Bryant, describing the situation as being between a “rock and a hard place”.

Speaking on Thursday night after the latest talks with the Orange Order and residents of Garvaghy Road broke up, Bryant said: “I think this is the end of these conversations. We haven’t come to a settled agreement, and it’s a shame, but my door remains open.”

Last Friday’s Parades Commission decision to grant the Orange Order the right to hold a procession down the nationalist Garvaghy Road plunged Northern Ireland into one of its most perilous periods since the 1998 peace deal.
A legal appeal by the Garvaghy Road Residents’ Coalition originally scheduled for Friday has been pushed back to Monday to facilitate any further talks.
“Obviously we’ll have to see how that plays out,” Bryant said, indicating he would not be intervening unilaterally. “I would say that the law, in the end, is the law.”

Five days of talks ended in deadlock, he said, outlining the compromises on the table for the first time. “We’ve discussed a wide range of options, including mediation, including an option where the right to march was respected but wasn’t exercised, including an option where there was a final march and no further applications for marches into the future, and we’ve not managed to come to agreement on any of all that.”

blocks.caption: Chris Bryant arrives at Hillsborough castle for talks on Thursday. Photograph: Liam McBurney/PA

blocks.text: Earlier in the week, reports suggested one option was a “one and done” parade involving just a dozen people without insignia in October. This would have been on condition the Orange Order would never apply for permit for that parade route again.
Breandán Mac Cionnaith, of the Garvaghy Road Residents’ Coalition said “the reality is” there was “no such thing as half a march”. “There’s a march or there’s not a march – simply that,” he said.
Jamie Bryson, a legal adviser to the Orange Order, who earlier this week said he would “not surrender” said he would accept Monday’s ruling.

“The challenge that we would put down to the Garvaghy Road residents – they’re going to the court of appeal on Monday – if the court of appeal upholds this determination, commit to accepting the law and walk away, and we’ll do the same,” he said. “Abide by the law, and if the court of appeal upholds the determination, get off the road, stop breaking the law and allow the parade to go ahead. If we lose, we’ll accept that.”

The dispute began last week after the march along the mainly nationalist Garvaghy Road was given the go-ahead by the Parades Commission for the first time since 1998, a decision denounced by Sinn Féin as “madness” and by the taoiseach as “incomprehensible and wrong”.

The dispute, which threatened to collapse Stormont and has returned Northern Ireland to bleak days of the past, has also revived the interest of key US Democrats. Richie Neal, the US representative for Massachussetts’ 1st congressional district, described the parade as “needlessly provocative”.
The Congressional Friends of Ireland Caucus, which Neal sits on, wrote to Bryant urging him to use his powers to reverse the Parades Commission decision.

“Over the last three decades, the progress made on the island of Ireland has been nothing short of extraordinary. Twenty-eight years have passed since the signing of the Good Friday agreement, and a generation has grown without a single memory of the Troubles,” the lawmakers wrote.

“Without decisive action, we risk reopening one of the most painful chapters of Northern Ireland’s history and undermining nearly three decades of peace, stability and reconciliation made possible by the Good Friday agreement.”
The Northern Ireland Policing Board has been told that the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) operation around the parading dispute has topped £3m.

articles.title: UK is not facing diesel shortage despite fears of Trump export ban, minister says
articles.summary: In effort to avoid panic at pumps, Keir Mather insists supply of fuel to Britain is ‘inherently resilient’

blocks.text: The government has moved to avert panic at the pumps, insisting that the UK is not facing a diesel shortage after Donald Trump threatened to cut off US supplies of the fuel.

The transport minister Keir Mather said on Friday that the UK has a wide range of sources of the fuel and is in talks with other European countries over the potential release of emergency diesel stockpiles.

“I want to reassure people that they can still go to the pump and fill up with diesel because the supply we have to the UK is inherently resilient,” he said, speaking on ITV’s Good Morning Britain. “The flows of diesel into the UK come from a variety of sources, and that is resilient. The government’s obligation now is to work really closely with our partners [in Europe] and officials in the US administration to re-stress how important it is to have flows of diesel into the UK.”
The UK relies on the US for about 30% of its diesel, with the vast majority coming from mainland Europe, and has reserve supplies for 42 days.

Earlier this week it emerged that the UK’s biggest refinery, Fawley in Hampshire, is set to shut down for up to 10 weeks for planned maintenance. The UK had 18 refineries in the 1980s but now has only four.

On Thursday the UK opened talks with European allies over releasing emergency diesel supplies, after the Trump administration told Germany and France to release their stockpiles to help ease soaring prices or face a US supply ban.
The average price of a litre of diesel in the UK hit an all-time high on Wednesday of 199.72p, according to the motoring body the RAC.

“Although prices have gone up at the pump, the government is aware of that, and the freeze in fuel duty is still in place,” Mather said. “People shouldn’t be concerned about shortages because of the inherent resilience that is built into that system.”
The government has extended the 5p cut in fuel duty until the end of the year. Earlier this week the RAC called on the government to extend the freeze into spring.

“We need to give people support where we can,” Mather said on GMB. “The government is not powerless. That is why we have a fuel duty freeze in place at the moment. The chancellor will set out the future of that at the budget, but is very aware of the impact that [high prices] are having on people.”
after newsletter promotion

On Friday, Dan Jørgensen, the EU commissioner for energy, said Europe was discussing the issue of whether to release emergency reserves of diesel with all members of the International Energy Agency, not only the US.
“This ‌is one of the ​opportunities that we have; we ⁠have used it before, ​and ​it is ​likely ​that ‌we ​would use ​it again,” he told Euronews.

articles.title: Trillanes unwelcome? A baseless assumption, says impeachment court spox
articles.summary: Former senator Sonny Trillanes claiming that he was not welcome to the Senate impeachment court is a “baseless assumption,” spokesperson Atty. Regie Tongol said Friday.

blocks.text: Published October 2, 2026 5:02pm
Former senator Sonny Trillanes claiming that he was not welcome to the Senate impeachment court is a “baseless assumption,” spokesperson Atty. Regie Tongol said Friday.

“Wala po, kasi wala naman pong ganyang pakiwari ang impeachment court at senator-judges kay former senator Trillanes. In fact, the fact na nakapasok nga siya nung Tuesday na nandun po siya at nakaupo po siya doon sa aming gallery kung saan ay nakalaan po iyon sa mga very important persons,” Tongol said in a press briefing.

(There is none, there is no sentiment like that from the impeachment court and the senator-judges regarding former senator Trillanes. The fact that he was able to come in last Tuesday and was able to sit in the gallery, which is designated for very important persons.)
“Walang ganoon na pinakita sa kanya ang impeachment court so I think that would be a baseless assumption kasi we have to base everything on the actions of the court,” he added.
(The impeachment court did not show anything like that to him so I think that would be a baseless assumption because we have to base everything on the actions of the court.)
Trillanes was among those named by the prosecution as their witness in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte but the impeachment court did not issue a subpoena for him.

The House prosecution panel said Thursday that they will no longer present the former senator as witness. Later in the day, Trillanes said it was he who asked the prosecution panel to withdraw his name
In a press conference Friday, Trillanes questioned why the impeachment court did not issue him a subpoena to testify for the prosecution.

"Sa akin kasi the signal is clear, hindi ako welcome. And by the way, hindi ito collective na parang sinasabi kasi ayaw daw ako ng mga senador. Inisa-isa natin 'yung mga naabutan natin doon. Hindi naman sila nakonsulta kaya next time na may magsabi na kasi may mga ano yung mga senador, don't swallow it right away,” he added.

(For me, the signal is clear: I was not welcome, but this is not a collective sentiment. There were comments that senators do not like me. I asked my former colleagues, and they said they weren’t consulted. So next time someone says senators don’t like me, don’t swallow it right away.)

Tongol explained that last Monday, Trillanes was supposed to be issued a subpoena. When the prosecution was asked who was going to be issued a subpoena, House prosecutor Terry Ridon did not mention the former senator.
The day after that, the prosecution mentioned that they wanted Trillanes to take a seat, but impeachment presiding officer Chiz Escudero could not issue a subpoena for the next day.
However, they could still have Trillanes as a voluntary witness. The presiding officer then warned the prosecution that they may be putting the cart before the horse, according to Tongol.
“Wala pa naman, at that time, na humingi sila na uupo na si former senator Trillanes, wala pang nape-presentang bank records noong panahon na 'yun, nung Tuesday,” Tongol said.
(At the time they were asking for former senator Trillanes to take a seat, no bank record has been presented yet.)
Tongol welcomed any criticisms from Trillanes regarding the court’s handling of the impeachment process, saying it is his freedom to do so. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Calls grow for US death penalty halt after ‘torturous’ botched execution of Christa Pike
articles.summary:
Pike alive but in critical condition as experts call ordeal that unfolded in Tennessee Wednesday ‘unimaginably barbaric’

Top lawyers, doctors and members of the faith community are calling…

blocks.text: Top lawyers, doctors and members of the faith community are calling for a moratorium on the US death penalty after Tennessee’s failed attempt to execute Christa Pike left the prisoner alive but in critical condition and receiving life-saving medical care.

The recent spate of harrowingly botched executions across US death penalty states reached a new low late on Wednesday when Tennessee’s governor Bill Lee called off the procedure after Pike had been injected with two full syringes of pentobarbital. She is the only person to have survived being administered 5mg of the sedative – a massive dose that under normal circumstances is considered fatal.

An hour after the first injection was given, she was overheard by eyewitnesses to be still breathing, choking and struggling, and was found to have a heartbeat. Her lawyers said that her current condition, and the degree to which she may have been brain damaged through oxygen deprivation, were as yet unknown.
Sandra Babcock, a death penalty scholar at Cornell law school who advises Pike’s legal team, told the Guardian that the events that unfolded were “unimaginably barbaric. They demand accountability.”
She added that at a minimum Lee must now “commute Christa Pike’s death sentence to life imprisonment”.

Another of Pike’s lawyers, Randy Spivey, who was present in the death chamber, called Pike’s ordeal “cruel and torturous”. He said he had personally counted seven needles stuck in Pike’s left arm alone, “one of which appeared to be bent when it was pulled from her”.
Pike, 50, was sentenced to death for the brutal 1995 killing of a teenage classmate, Colleen Slemmer. She was set to be the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years.

Leading voices on the death penalty in America told the Guardian that the failed execution was such a violation of the constitutional prohibition on “cruel and unusual punishment” that all judicial killings had to be halted. Bryan Stevenson, an internationally renowned death penalty lawyer and founder of the Equal Justice Initiative in Montgomery, Alabama, said that many warnings had been made in recent months that US executions were flawed and unreliable.
“Nearly a dozen botched executions in recent years should have suspended executions long before now,” he said.

Stevenson said it was time to turn around the threshold question. Instead of asking whether a prisoner deserved to die for the crime committed, the question should be: “Do our governments which tolerate inequality, unreliability and bias deserve to kill?”
He added: “Last night’s tragedy makes clear we should stop the misguided policy of killing people to show that killing is wrong.”

Wednesday night was the second time in five months that Tennessee had failed an execution. In May, Tony Carruthers survived the death chamber after the execution team were unable to set up an IV line.
He has been given a new execution date for next May.

That followed Alabama, which also failed to execute two death row prisoners, Alan Miller and Kenneth Smith, having been unable to find a vein. The spectacle of prisoners being sent to their deaths, only to have the executions called off as a result of basic failures in IV procedures, has sent death penalty states scrambling to find alternatives to lethal injections.

In turn, those alternative procedures have become mired in complications and disputes. Miller and Smith were both eventually killed by Alabama using an experimental procedure, nitrogen gas, that veterinarians have banned as inhumane for the euthanasia of cats and dogs.
In June, a federal judge blocked Alabama’s use of nitrogen in executions, ruling it cruel and unusual punishment.

Other states have opted for the firing squad. But recent firing squad executions have been troubled by bullets missing the heart, to the extent that the suggestion has been raised that some of the mis-targeted shots might have been intentional.

Helen Prejean, a Catholic nun who is perhaps the best-known advocate for abolition of the death penalty in America after her book Dead Man Walking was turned into a film of the same name, told the Guardian that the events on Wednesday night were the definition of cruelty.

“This is the essence of cruelty. Take a conscious, imaginative human being, give her a date for her death, have her anticipate it over and over again, and then take her out and try and kill her. She was rendered defenceless as they deliberately attempted to kill her – what greater mental torture for a human being is there?”
Prejean added that she hoped the agony Pike had endured “would be redemptive for others, and help to wake up the nation”.

As the number of gruesome botched lethal injections rapidly mounts, the central premise that has been held up by supporters – that it is a humane, medicalised and scientific way to kill a person – has come under fire. Joel Zivot, a professor of anesthesiology in Atlanta, Georgia, who has reviewed hundreds of autopsies of executed people in the US, said that lethal injections would never deserve the label of medicine.
“This is the impersonation of a medical act. It is the theft of a medical act. So when it goes awry, that is not at all surprising to me.”

Zivot was invited to present as an expert witness at a hearing convened in August by a special master in the Pike case. He warned the senior judge that Pike had a blood condition in which her blood platelets were elevated that rendered her vulnerable to blood clots.

Zivot told the hearing that Pike, as a small woman who had been in solitary confinement on death row for almost 30 years, likely had veins that were of poor quality, small in caliber, and hard to find. “I told them. I warned them,” he said.
The special master rejected almost all the evidence presented to him.

The last time that the US saw a moratorium on executions was in 1972 when the supreme court ruled in Furman v Georgia that capital punishment was capricious and arbitrary in its rendition. The ban was lifted four years later.

Paradoxically, calls for a renewed nationwide pause are reaching fever pitch at precisely the time that pressure to carry out executions is also peaking. Donald Trump has repeatedly exhorted death penalty states and the federal Department of Justice to speed up judicial killings, and his orders are having an effect.
Last year saw the highest number of US executions – 47 across 12 states – in 16 years.

Prejean said that the answer to the growing determination of Trump and the death penalty states to carry out executions was to bring the American people closer to the action. She pointed to Gallup’s findings tracking popular sentiment towards capital punishment.
In 1993, when her book came out, 80% of Americans supported the death penalty for convicted murderers. Now that figure is 52%.

“That’s progress, though not enough. People have good hearts, but they are too removed from the process that is secret and hidden. We have got to bring this to the people, bring them into the execution chamber, so that they too become a witness.”

articles.title: Eastern Spain braces for torrential rain and flooding
articles.summary:
Up to 300mm of rain could fall in places, while extreme downpours bring deadly landslides to Nepal

Torrential rain and potentially damaging flooding are forecast in eastern Spain over the…
articles.byline: Megan Davies and James Michelin for MetDesk

blocks.text: Torrential rain and potentially damaging flooding are forecast in eastern Spain over the coming days, as cold upper air moves over the warm, humid surface air of the Mediterranean Sea, fuelling violent, slow-moving thunderstorms near Spain’s east coast. The weather pattern, known as a Dana, occurs most often in autumn.

Models show more than 100mm of rain could fall across the region on Friday, with 200-300mm possible in some areas. Cities including Valencia and Castelló de la Plana, with Valencia having experienced several damaging floods in recent years, are most at risk. Catalonia has now put three towns under lockdown and Valencia has shut schools for nearly half a million children.

Meanwhile, heavy rainfall in Nepal this week resulted in 542 disaster incidents and left 27 people dead between 24 and 27 September, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority. Of the recorded incidents, 304 were related to landslides while 87 were linked to flooding.

blocks.caption: A woman and child displaced by flash floods and mudslides in Nuwakot district, Nepal. Photograph: Adnan Abidi/Reuters

blocks.text: During this extremely wet period, 186 meteorological sites recorded more than 100mm of rainfall, with Dedhgaun, in Lumbini province, recording 544.2mm. Nearly a million people received SMS flood warnings, and 2,000 people living in high-risk areas were relocated.

This heavy rainfall also affected the Gandak River in Bihar, north-east India, which reached a record water level of 91.25 metres on Tuesday, 0.35m metres above the previous record, set only in 2024, according to the water resources department. So far, 169 seepage points along the embankments have been repaired, with teams deployed across several sites along the river as the embankments continue to face heavy water pressure.

Strong winds, heavy rainfall and coastal flooding have hit the north-east US as a very deep area of low pressure developed into a nor’easter on Saturday. Such storms are named due to the north-easterly winds typically affecting coastal areas. This was the first nor’easter of the autumn/winter season, bringing gusts of up to 74mph (119km/h) and waves rising to 3 metres.

The storm left approximately 200,000 people without power, inundated the streets of New York City and killed one person when a tree fell in Brooklyn. However, the storm also uncovered a piece of history as the wreckage from the Warren Sawyer, a three-masted ship destroyed in 1884, washed ashore on Nantucket, off Cape Cod in Massachusetts.

articles.title: Row erupts over Cairo mural depicting Tutankhamun and Nefertiti with dark skin
articles.summary:
Artwork created in Tahrir Square for Chinese president’s state visit to Egypt is painted over amid allegations it revived Afrocentric claims about Pharaohs’ origins

On the…

blocks.text: On the eve of Chinese president Xi Jinping’s state visit to Cairo last month, the city authorities were busy removing a 66-metre-long mural from the esteemed guest’s line of sight.

Depicting the Pharaoh Tutankhamun and Queen Nefertiti, the painting was among 40 murals commissioned to beautify the city for Xi’s arrival and was painted by volunteer youth group Rasmet Basma, in Tahrir Square.

But it drew a furious reaction for depicting the two historical figures with dark skin – angering those Egyptians who saw it as reviving Afrocentric claims about the Pharaohs’ origins. The artwork vanished under fresh paint just hours before Xi landed.
Now, Ahmed Moussa, the 22-year-old founder of Rasmet Basma, has admitted it was asked by the Cairo governorate to paint over its work, which had been prepared in just five days in late August.

blocks.caption: Volunteer Razan Mujahid works on the mural. Photograph: Rasmet Basma

blocks.text: The team used the AI programme ChatGPT to generate the designs, which volunteers then painted on to the wall.
Moussa said Cairo’s deputy governor and the head of the district had visited the site throughout the process and were impressed by the murals – until controversy began to build on social media.
“We used a golden-bronze tone that cast a kind of shadow on the faces at night, so they appeared dark-skinned,” Moussa said.
“We acknowledge our mistake in not consulting specialists in archaeology and art.”
Afrocentrism is a political movement asserting that ancient Egyptian civilisation was black African in origin and population.

One user asked whether anyone involved had “even seen what Nefertiti actually looked like”, while others accused Afrocentric groups of appropriating the images to claim Egyptians endorsed their theories.

Zahi Hawass, Egypt’s former antiquities minister, said the volunteers should not have been allowed to paint a city site as significant as Tahrir Square without expert oversight, and that the public outrage was justified.
“Claims linking ancient Egyptian civilisation to sub-Saharan Africa are nonsense,” Hawass said.
“Temple carvings from the late period show Egyptian kings depicted alongside captives from parts of Africa, Libya, Syria and Palestine, with the king himself not shown as dark-skinned,” he said.

blocks.caption: The mural has reignited a debate about the complexion of ancient Egyptians. Photograph: Rasmet Basma

blocks.text: This is just the latest episode in a long-running debate over the complexion of ancient Egyptians. In 2023, a Netflix documentary provoked discussion after casting a dark-skinned actor as Cleopatra, and a similar dispute flared in June 2024 after a guide reportedly gave an Afrocentric perspective of Egyptian history in Cairo’s Egyptian Museum.

Monica Hanna, an Egyptologist at the American University in Cairo, labelled Afrocentric claims “pseudoscience”. She said Egyptian society had always been ethnically diverse, from Nubian communities in the south to Mediterranean populations in the north.
“Egyptians were never one skin colour,” she said. “We are not snow-white, or the colour of cream.”

Walid Mahmoud, an AI researcher and expert in African anthropology, said AI tools such as ChatGPT reflected whatever information was most widely shared online, rather than what was factually accurate.
They were built by companies in the US and Europe, he said, and the content they generated could shape how those audiences saw themselves.

blocks.caption: The mural was repainted white just hours before President Xi landed in Egypt. Photograph: Hanaa Hammad

blocks.text: “That’s why we should never simply accept what it produces, especially when it comes to cultural identity and heritage,” Mahmoud said.
Mostafa Eissa, an art critic, said AI should remain a tool, never a decision-maker in its own right.

“I favour using technology without abandoning the human element within the artist,” he said, warning that letting such tools substitute an artist’s own skill risked emptying a work of its originality.

articles.title: Badenoch claims Labour is preparing for a general election in May 2027 – UK politics live
articles.summary:
Speculation about an early election continue to persist even as Andy Burnham ruled it out

Zack Polanski is expected to call for a triple lock-style guarantee for private renters at…

blocks.text: Badenoch claims Labour preparing for a May 2027 general election
Hello and welcome to the UK politics live blog.
Tory leader Kemi Badenoch says Labour is preparing for a general election as early as May 2027, despite the prime minister ruling out an early contest.
Just last week Andy Burnham said he would not call a national vote before 2029, despite speculation that Labour’s revival in the polls could tempt him to go early.
But Badenoch said the fact that so many of the pledges in his conference speech would not come into place until after the next general election points to a spring vote.
Ahead of the Conservative party conference next week, the leader of the opposition said: “We could be having a general election next May.”
She added:

double quotation markAll the policies he announced are for after an election. So if he’s not calling an election, why is he talking about things happening in 2030? He says a lot of things with a smile but I actually think that he’s got very different plans for us and for our country.
double quotation markThis is an era of political volatility and multi-party politics. When an election is called and I do think Andy Burnham is going to call an election sooner than he is saying.

Talk of an early election had grown during the last week after polls showed Labour pulling into the lead with support in the low 20s, and the Conservatives and Reform neck-and-neck a few points behind them.

Westminster sources said Downing Street advisers and MPs had been discussing the merits of an early poll but that even though the right was split, Labour would be at risk of losing its majority and having to form a coalition.
In other developments:

blocks.text: Polanski to use conference speech to call for triple lock-style guarantee to limit rent rises
Zack Polanski is expected to call for a triple lock-style guarantee for private renters at his party’s annual conference in Brighton today, to ease young adults’ housing costs.

The Green party leader’s speech will set out plans for a “three-year emergency brake”, which would temporarily limit rent rises to the lowest of either Consumer Prices Index (CPI) inflation, wage growth or 2%.

“For too long, landlords have been able to hike prices way beyond wages,” Polanski is expected to say. He will describe “25-year-olds who can’t find a job, no matter how many tens or hundreds of applications they put in, who can’t imagine ever being able to afford to rent even a room of their own, never mind being able to put down roots in their own home”.

The party leader will also describe “30, 35-year-olds moving back to their parents’ place with their partners in tow, sometimes their kids too”, warning that for many of them “times get tougher and those months turn to years”.
Polanski is expected to say:

double quotation markToday I’m calling for a three-year emergency brake on private rents – no rent rises above CPI, wage growth or 2% – whichever is lower. No sudden hikes, no evictions under the guise of rent rises, no more fear and uncertainty. That emergency brake would give renters vital breathing space. Let wages begin to catch up with the rents that have outstripped them for too long. And give government time to develop a national fair rents guarantee – to keep rents fair and affordable for everyone, forever.

articles.title: Senate bill eyes to lower age for SK voting, candidacy to 15-21 years old
articles.summary: From 18 to 24 years old, the proposed measure seeks to lower the age requirement to 15 to 21 years old.

blocks.text: People gesture after casting their votes during the presidential election at a polling station in Manila on May 9, 2022.
AFP / Chaideer Mahyuddin
MANILA, Philippines — A measure seeking to lower the age of eligible voters and candidates for Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) is being pushed in the Senate.

Senate Bill No. 2510 introduced by Sen. Vicente ‘Tito’ Sotto III is pushing to lower the age of young adults who are eligible to vote and run for positions in barangay’s youth council by amending Section 10 of the Republic Act No. 10742 or the Sangguniang Kabataan Reform Act of 2015.
From 18 to 24 years old, the proposed measure seeks to lower the age requirement to 15 to 21 years old.
In the bill’s explanatory note, Sotto said there is a need to bring back the SK mechanism to the youth sector and noted the importance of teaching children good governance.
“They are the voice and the representation of the youth in our governance framework, especially to the unit of government that is closest to the people,” Sotto said.

The bill comes a week after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. approved Republic Act No. 12326 which postponed the supposed barangay and SK elections on November 2 this year, moving it to the first Monday of November 2028.
No hard infra projects

Sotto’s proposed measure is also seeking to prohibit the SK funds to be used for procurement of hard infrastructure projects and high value properties that are higher than one-fourths of their annual budget.

“The Sangguniang Kabataan shall be prohibited from participating and their funds shall not be utilized in the procurement of hard infrastructure projects and high value properties where the amount of which exceeds 25% of their annual budget,” the proposed additional paragraph on Section 20 of Republic Act No. 10742 read.

The proposed additional paragraph, moreover, says the development plan of the youth council shall be strictly followed in the procurement process, saying any goods or properties not indicated in the plan shall not be purchased “unless a notarized justification in writing is submitted.”

“This bill aims to lower the age of qualification to run in the Sangguniang Kabataan and provide mechanisms that will deter corrupt practices and to allow the youth to be developed as effective leaders and to lead their fellow youth through the Sanggunian,” Sotto said.
Amendments on SK functions
Aside from lowering the age of eligible voters and officers, the bill is also pushing amendments related to SK funds and functions.

Sotto is seeking to limit the scope of plans and programs indicated in the Comprehensive Barangay Youth Development Plan, or the three-year rolling plan that the youth council must develop upon their assumption in office.

“The plans and programs to be indicated therein shall be limited to advocacy and campaigns, information and education, sports and physical development, welfare and support systems, and such other programs geared towards supporting the youth within their jurisdiction,” the proposed amendment read.

Plans and programs, it added, shall focus on good governance, climate change adaptation and environmental protection, disaster risk reduction, health services, anti-drug abuse, gender sensitivity, sports development, accessible education, sustainable development, human rights advocacy, and social protection.

articles.title: Recent lobbyist for Palantir had key role in helping Andy Burnham become PM
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Martha Dalton worked closely with Burnham’s team on byelection that secured his return to parliament

A recent lobbyist for the controversial $450bn US tech company Palantir played…

blocks.text: A recent lobbyist for the controversial $450bn US tech company Palantir played a senior role in helping Andy Burnham become prime minister, it has emerged.

Martha Dalton, whose company Lodestone worked for Palantir in 2024 and 2025, campaigned for Burnham in the Makerfield byelection that secured his return to parliament. She worked closely with his team on strategic communications and rebuttals, and was among supporters who clapped him into Downing Street in July.

Lodestone, which Dalton co-founded, worked for Palantir on projects including promoting its software at events in parliament where its engineers demonstrated AI-powered systems for use in British public services to MPs.
Dalton previously worked on the autumn 2025 deputy leadership campaign for the current education secretary, Lucy Powell, a few months after Lodestone stopped working for Palantir.
Her role emerged as Palantir fights to retain its £330m contract with NHS England to run the federated data platform, a national medical data system.

Burnham’s government is under pressure to scrap the deal. Campaigners are angry about Palantir’s work for the Israeli military in Gaza and Donald Trump’s ICE immigration crackdown. They have also raised concerns, acknowledged by NHS England’s chief executive, Jim Mackey, that the benefits to public health may not be as significant as has been claimed.

blocks.caption: Health workers protest against Palantir outside the company’s London headquarters on Wednesday.  Photograph: Vuk Valcic/Zuma Press Wire/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Lodestone’s work for Palantir and Dalton’s subsequent role with Burnham is the latest link between Labour and the tech firm, which also works for the US and UK militaries and was co-founded by the Trump-supporting tech billionaire Peter Thiel.

The Labour peer Tom Watson took a full-time job lobbying for Palantir earlier this month after a period as a member of Lodestone’s “strategic advisory council”. Palantir previously employed Peter Mandelson’s lobbying firm, Global Counsel, before it collapsed over the former Labour trade secretary’s links to Jeffrey Epstein.

Dalton wrote on her LinkedIn account that it had been “an absolute honour to work on Andy Burnham’s campaign to become Labour leader and prime minister”. She took six weeks’ unpaid leave from Lodestone to spend time in Makerfield “supporting on strategic comms and rebuttals”.

A spokesperson for Lodestone said: “She had no contact with clients during that time and did so because she believes Andy Burnham is the best person to lead the Labour party and the country. Lodestone had previously worked with Palantir on various projects – all focused on helping them to explain their technology to those who rightly hold them to account.”

Health workers who want ministers to scrap Palantir’s NHS deal protested at the Labour party conference in Liverpool on Tuesday. Labour members had earlier tabled a motion calling for the deal to be axed, claiming Palantir was “facing numerous allegations of involvement in serious breaches of human rights”, citing its development of technology for Israel’s military.

Palantir’s executive vice-president for the UK and Europe, Louis Mosley, has said its technology was used to locate hostages but not to identify military targets in Gaza. That appears to contradict an earlier statement by the firm’s chief executive, Alex Karp, who was challenged last year by a protester alleging “Palantir kills Palestinians” in Gaza. He replied: “Mostly terrorists, that’s true.”
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: Palantir’s chief executive, Alex Karp. Photograph: Andrew Thomas/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Palantir’s fortunes in the UK are intertwined with the Labour government. A break clause in the NHS England contract looms in February 2027. The Labour mayor of London, Sadiq Khan, is also in a legal battle with Palantir after he blocked the Metropolitan police from awarding it a £50m contract to supply AI tools to assist criminal investigations. The firm also has a £240m contract with the Ministry of Defence and has been selling its services to other police forces and councils.

Mosley recently said that people who don’t recognise the positive impact the firm’s technology has on cutting treatment waiting times and speeding up hospital discharges were suffering from “Palantir derangement syndrome”.

Tom Brake, the chief executive of Unlock Democracy, a not-for-profit campaign group, said candidates should observe Cabinet Office advice on secondments before adding volunteers or secondees to their campaign teams.
“This requires successful secondees to declare relevant outside interests, clarify that potential conflicts will be explored and ensure appropriate mitigations are put in place,” he said.
A Labour spokesperson said: “There are robust rules and procedures to manage any potential conflicts, whether that be in government or in campaigns, and those were followed.”

A Palantir spokesperson said: “Lodestone has worked with us on a range of projects to explain how our software is used to deliver public services – for example parliamentary events that enable MPs to see demonstrations of our software and ask our engineers questions around data privacy and security.”
